honor.en: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent

translationRepairs: Xiao Yu; his nephew's son Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.

Xiao Yu; his nephew Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.
從子 is a nephew, not a nephew’s son.
When the Prince of Jin was made crown prince, Yu was appointed Right Thousand-Bull.
When the Prince of Jin was made crown prince, Yu was appointed an officer of the Right Qianniu Guard.
右千牛 is an officer of the Right Qianniu (Thousand Ox) Guard.

On his accession the consort became empress, and Yu grew ever closer in the emperor's favor, rising in turn to Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe and acting Eagle-Brand commandant of the Left Wing Guard.

On his accession the consort became empress, and Yu grew ever closer in the emperor's favor, rising in turn to Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe and acting Hawk-Soaring Commandant of the Left Flanking Guard.
鷹揚郎將 is the Hawk-Soaring Commandant; 左翊衛 the Left Flanking Guard.
Appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, he often spoke against the emperor's wishes and gradually fell under suspicion.
Appointed vice director of the Secretariat, he often spoke against the emperor's wishes and gradually fell under suspicion.
內史侍郎 is vice director of the Secretariat.

When Gaozu entered the capital he summoned Yu, who brought his commandery and submitted; he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Song, and made Minister of the Household.
When Gaozu entered the capital he summoned Yu, who brought his commandery and submitted; he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Song, and made Minister of Revenue.
民部尚書 is the Minister of Revenue.
That year the prefecture was given seven offices; the Prince of Qin became governor of Yongzhou and Yu was made regional commander.
That year the prefecture was given seven offices; the Prince of Qin became governor of Yongzhou and Yu was made area commander-in-chief of the prefecture.
州都督 is the area commander-in-chief.
After more than a year he was recalled as regional commander of Jin.
After more than a year he was recalled as area commander-in-chief of Jinzhou.
晉州都督 is area commander-in-chief of Jinzhou.
Recalled to court he was made minister of rites, then censor-in-chief, and took part in government deliberations.
Recalled to court he was made Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then censor-in-chief, and took part in government deliberations.
太常卿 heads the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

When Fang Xuanling and others committed minor faults Yu impeached them harshly; the emperor did not act, and Yu thereby lost standing; he was made junior tutor to the heir apparent with special advancement, then again minister of rites.

When Fang Xuanling and others committed minor faults Yu impeached them harshly; the emperor did not act, and Yu thereby lost standing; he was made junior mentor to the heir apparent with special advancement, then again Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
太子少傅 is junior mentor (distinct from 少師); 太常卿 is the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Yu was appointed grand tutor to the heir apparent and associate grand councilor of the third rank.
When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Yu was appointed grand guardian of the heir apparent and associate grand councilor of the third rank.
太子太保 is the grand guardian, not the grand tutor.
An edict posthumously granted him minister of works and regional commander of Jing, with burial at Zhaoling.
An edict posthumously granted him Grand Minister of Works and area commander-in-chief of Jingzhou, with burial at Zhaoling.
司空 is the Grand Minister of Works; 荊州都督 the area commander-in-chief of Jingzhou.
The Ministry of Rites proposed the posthumous name Su; because of his jealous nature the emperor changed it to Zhenbian (Upright but Narrow).
The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Su; because of his jealous nature the emperor changed it to Zhenbian (Upright but Narrow).
太常 is the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
His son Rui married Princess Xiangcheng and served as vice minister of rites.
His son Rui married Princess Xiangcheng and served as vice chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
太常少卿 is vice chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Jun, Yu's nephew's son, was talented and well regarded.
Jun, Yu's nephew, was talented and well regarded.
During the Yonghui era he rose to remonstrating censor and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
During the Yonghui era he rose to Grand Master of Remonstrance and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
諫議大夫 is the Grand Master of Remonstrance.
The emperor said, "A true remonstrating censor!"
諫議 refers to his remonstrance post, not a censor.
A craftsman of the Ministry of Rites carried messages and gifts for palace women; an edict ordered his execution under the applicable statute.
A craftsman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices carried messages and gifts for palace women; an edict ordered his execution under the applicable statute.
太常工 is a craftsman of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
The emperor said, "When Ruji stole the tally I took it as a warning; I will not put the craftsman to death without cause, yet I am glad to receive loyal counsel."
The emperor said, "When Lady Ruji stole the tally I took it as a warning; I will not put the craftsman to death without cause, yet I am glad to receive loyal counsel."
如姬 is Lady Ruji of Wei.
He ended his career as director of the heir apparent's directorate of palace supplies.
He ended his career as Director of the Heir Apparent's Office of the Watches.
太子率更令 heads the office of timekeeping, not palace supplies.
His son Guan served as secretary-general of Yu; while mourning his mother he died from grief-induced exhaustion.
His son Guan served as secretary-general of Yuzhou; while mourning his mother he died from grief-induced exhaustion.
渝州 is Yuzhou, not Xiao Yu.
He rose to minister of ceremonies and concurrently secretary-general of the Chanyu Protectorate.
He rose to Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and concurrently secretary-general of the Chanyu Protectorate.
鴻臚卿 heads the Court of State Ceremonial.

Early on he married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji. His colleague by marriage Lu Xiangxian, son of a chief minister and then magistrate of Luoyang, was already famous, and men rushed to befriend him; Song, obscure and still without office, drew no special notice.

Early on he married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji. His brother-in-law Lu Xiangxian, whose wife was his wife’s sister,, son of a chief minister and then commandant of Luoyang, was already famous, and men rushed to befriend him; Song, obscure and still without office, drew no special notice.
僚婿 are men married to sisters. 洛陽尉 is the commandant of Luoyang.
Jiang Shidu, the Hebei promotion and demotion commissioner, recommended him as judge.
Jiang Shidu, the Hebei promotion and demotion commissioner, recommended him as his administrative assistant.
判官 is an administrative assistant to a commissioner.
He served as prefect of Song and was transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
He served as prefect of Songzhou and was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
宋州 is Songzhou; 尚書左丞 is the left assistant director.
About then the Tibetan generals Sinolucigonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi captured Guazhou and took the prefect Tian Yuanxian prisoner;
About then the Tibetan generals Xinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi captured Guazhou and took the prefect Tian Yuanxian prisoner;
悉諾邏恭祿 is romanized Xinuoluo Gonglu.
Sinolucigonglu then dominated the tribal confederations, and Tibet used his prowess to harry the frontier. Song sowed discord and planted doubts until the Tibetan king had him put to death.
Xinuoluo Gonglu then dominated the tribal confederations, and Tibet used his prowess to harry the frontier. Song sowed discord and planted doubts until the Tibetan king had him put to death.
悉諾邏恭祿 is romanized Xinuoluo Gonglu.
Song recommended Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, made Zhang Shougui of the Jian'ang army prefect of Guazhou, rebuilt walls and forts, and looked after the frontier population.
Song recommended Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, made Zhang Shougui of the Jiankang army prefect of Guazhou, rebuilt walls and forts, and looked after the frontier population.
建康軍 is the Jiankang army.

When Zhang Zhiliang, governor of Zheng, routed the enemy west of Qinghai, Song sent his deputy Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight the Tibetans at Qilian City. From dawn until evening they battled; the Tibetans broke utterly, a general was killed, and their laments echoed through the ravines.

When Zhang Zhiliang, area commander-in-chief of Shanzhou, routed the enemy west of Qinghai, Song sent his deputy Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight the Tibetans at Qilian City. From dawn until evening they battled; the Tibetans broke utterly, a general was killed, and their laments echoed through the ravines.
鄯州都督 is the area commander-in-chief of Shanzhou.
In the seventeenth year he was further appointed chief of the Secretariat.
In the seventeenth year he was further appointed Director of the Secretariat.
中書令 is the Director of the Secretariat.
Since Zhang Yue had left office, the chief ministership had stood empty for four years; Song finally held it, but continued to hold the Hexi command remotely.
Since Zhang Yue had left office, the directorship of the Secretariat had stood empty for four years; Song finally held it, but continued to hold the Hexi command remotely.
令 here is the 中書令 post.
Go home, brother—tonight you will receive an edict."
Just go home—tonight you will receive an edict."
弟 here stands for 第, "just"; it is not "brother".
Song was made Right Chief of the Department of State Affairs, and both he and Xiu left the chief ministry.
Song was made Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, and both he and Xiu left the chief ministry.
尚書右丞相 is the right chancellor of the department.
He promoted his son Hua to Drafting Attendant.
He promoted his son Hua to Supervising Secretary.
給事中 is the supervising secretary.
In time he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
In time he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
太子太師 is the grand preceptor.
He was soon restored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
He was soon restored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
太子太師 is the grand preceptor.

Zhang Shougui of Youzhou was punished for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong. Li Linfu, who had long envied Song, claimed Song had once given his south-city villa to Xiantong, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.

Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Youzhou, was punished for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong. Li Linfu, who had long envied Song, claimed Song had once given his south-city villa to Xiantong, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.
幽州節度使 is the military commissioner of Youzhou.
He died in Tianbao 8 (749) and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with parity to the Three Excellencies.
He died in Tianbao 8 (749) and was posthumously honored as Unequalled in Honor with parity to the Three Excellencies.
開府儀同三司 is not 光祿大夫; it is the Kaifu yitong sansi dignity.
After the rout at Xiang, Hua returned to court but, tainted by his surrender to the rebels, was provisionally made Junior Mentor of the Secretariat.
After the rout at Xiang, Hua returned to court but, tainted by his surrender to the rebels, was provisionally made acting Vice Director of the Palace Library.
試秘書少監 is acting vice director of the Palace Library.
He rose to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then to military commissioner of Hedong over Jin and Jiang.
He rose to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, then to military commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
尚書右丞 is right assistant director; 河中晉絳 is Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
Daizong was then in mourning; Yuan Zai aided Fuguo, demoted Hua to militia-commander of Xia, and Hua died.
Daizong was then in mourning; Yuan Zai aided Fuguo, demoted Hua to adjutant of Xiazhou, and Hua died.
峽州司馬 is the adjutant of Xiazhou.
He secured for him the yin privilege appointment as palace gate officer.
Through the princess’s yin privilege he was made palace gate officer.
推主廕 means via the princess’s hereditary privilege.
Before he could depart, the court fled to Fengtian.
Before he could depart, he accompanied the emperor’s flight to Fengtian.
扈狩奉天: Fu escorted the emperor to Fengtian.

Sheng died young. The princess was twice disgraced and deposed over witchcraft; her sons were sent to remote exile; her daughter married the crown prince, who sought divorce. The emperor still nursed old grievances, and Fu was demoted to acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and exiled to Raozhou.

Sheng died young. The princess was twice disgraced and deposed over witchcraft; her sons were sent to remote exile; her daughter married the crown prince, who sought divorce. The emperor still nursed old grievances, and Fu was demoted to acting Senior Secretary of the Left to the Heir Apparent and exiled to Raozhou.
太子左庶子 is the senior secretary of the left.
Fu aspired to the prestige of great houses, held fast to honor, and kept his distance from the coarse world.
Fu came from an eminent and illustrious lineage, held fast to honor, and kept his distance from the coarse world.
望閥高華 describes his lineage, not an aspiration.
Huangfu Bo had him appointed Censor-in-Chief.
Huangfu Bo had him appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
御史中丞 is the vice censor-in-chief.
Bo and Linghu Chu both favored Mian; as co-regents they praised him often, and the emperor treated him with marked regard.
Bo and Linghu Chu both favored Mian; as fellow chief ministers they praised him often, and the emperor treated him with marked regard.
同輔政 means jointly serving as chief ministers.
He then shunned personnel matters, was moved to the Ministry of War, and pleaded illness for a sinecure in Luoyang; the request was denied.
He then shunned personnel matters, was moved to Minister of War, and pleaded illness for a sinecure in Luoyang; the request was denied.
徙兵部 is a transfer to minister of war.
He was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Tongzhou.
He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Tongzhou.
太子少保 is the junior guardian.
He later served in Luoyang in the same nominal capacity.
He later served as Junior Guardian with a branch post in the Eastern Capital, Luoyang.
以少保分司東都 makes the office explicit.
He eventually rose to Supervising Censor.
He eventually rose to Supervising Secretary.

Later Fang was liable to punishment because the returned edict was damaged. Kong Wenyü, a lecturer at court, argued, "A Supervising Censor's objections weigh right and wrong for the state—they are not ordinary bureaucratic papers and should not be penalized."

Later Fang was liable to punishment because of errors in the edict he had sealed and returned. Kong Wenyü, Academician Lecturer-in-Waiting, argued, "A Supervising Secretary's objections weigh right and wrong for the state—they are not ordinary bureaucratic papers and should not be penalized."
封敕脫誤 means errors in the returned edict. 侍講學士 is academician lecturer-in-waiting; 給事中 is supervising secretary.

Linghu Tao had Li Zhuo pacify Annan; Zhuo was dismissed for brutality and sloth but soon resurfaced as commander at Shouzhou. Fang impeached him without flinching, and contemporaries admired his integrity.

Linghu Tao had Li Zhuo pacify Annan; Zhuo was dismissed for brutality and sloth but soon resurfaced as militia commissioner of Shouzhou. Fang impeached him without flinching, and contemporaries admired his integrity.
壽州團練使 is militia commissioner.
Early in the Xiantong era he became Left Regular Attendant.
Early in the Xiantong era he became Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
左散騎常侍. is the correct office title here.
He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor and Marquis of Lanling.
He was further promoted to Minister of Works and Marquis of Lanling.
司空 is minister of works.
He passed the jinshi and was appointed a Secretariat official.
He passed the jinshi and was appointed a department official of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書郎. is the correct office title here.
When Lingzi resisted Huang Chao he named Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to registrar at Hezhou.
When Lingzi resisted Huang Chao he named Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to revenue section administrator of Hezhou.
司戶參軍事. is the correct office title here.
In the Guanghua era he was recalled as Supervising Censor but did not come; he died.
In the Guanghua era he was recalled as Supervising Secretary but did not come; he died.
給事中. is the correct office title here.
Baoheng was mediocre, and the literati held him in low regard, yet they alone addressed Gou as Grand Marshal—a slight Baoheng resented.
Baoheng was mediocre, and the literati held him in low regard, yet they alone addressed Gou as Grand Commandant—a slight Baoheng resented.
太尉. is the correct office title here.
By then Baoheng was chief minister; he dredged up charges against Gou and banished him from his post as Palace Diary Attendant to military adjutant at distant Bozhou.
By then Baoheng was chief minister; he dredged up charges against Gou and banished him from his post as Palace Diary Attendant to aide (sima) of distant Bozhou.
播州司馬. is the correct office title here.
Before long Baoheng died, and Gou was recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
Before long Baoheng died, and Gou was recalled as Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites.
禮部員外郎. is the correct office title here.
In the Qianfu era he rose to Vice Director of Revenue and Expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
In the Qianfu era he rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and Recipient of Edicts of the Hanlin Academy.
戶部侍郎、翰林學士承旨.

At Xuzhou, Governor Zhi Xiang had taken on Li Sun's son Ningji as his aide. A junior officer, Shi Bo, drove Xiang out and seized the command. Bo was poisoned by a kitchen steward but survived; someone then accused Ningji of plotting revenge on Xiang's behalf, and Bo had him killed in a fury.

At Xuzhou, Governor Zhi Xiang had taken on Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Sun's son Ningji as his aide. A junior officer, Shi Bo, drove Xiang out and seized the command. Bo was poisoned by a kitchen steward but survived; someone then accused Ningji of plotting revenge on Xiang's behalf, and Bo had him killed in a fury.
On returning to Chang'an, Mei made Changtu chief minister to the new emperor and stripped Gou of his rank, making him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
On returning to Chang'an, Mei made Changtu chief minister to the new emperor and stripped Gou of his rank, making him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
太子太保 is the grand guardian of the heir apparent.
He entered service through hereditary privilege as adjutant at Shanzhou and magistrate of Jincheng.
He entered service through hereditary privilege as adjutant at Shanzhou and assistant magistrate of Jincheng.
金城丞 is an assistant magistrate post.
He rose to director in the Left and Right Secretariats.
He rose to Director of the Left and Right Offices of the Department of State Affairs.
左右司郎中 are the left and right office directors.
After order was restored, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
After order was restored, he was made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
太子少師 is the junior preceptor.
He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
太子太師 is the grand preceptor.
candidateDispositions: Contextual: Wei is the Weibo region, not Lady Wei.
Contextual: Heaven here is the cosmic sky, not the Son of Heaven.
Contextual: Heaven here is the cosmic sky, not the Son of Heaven.
Contextual: Song here is the fief in Duke of Song, not Xiao Song.
Contextual: Jin here is the Jin dynasty.
Contextual: Yu here is Yuzhou (渝州), not Xiao Yu.
Contextual: Jin here is Jinzhou, not Wang Jin.
Contextual: a deity worshipped at a shrine, not a historical person.
Contextual: a deity worshipped at a shrine, not a historical person.
